Immersive Technology

By: James Carroll | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
we dive in to the immersive world of virtual reality

Unique Selling Point:
Potentially the first insert to be shot on a 360 camera rig for Carte Blanche so viewers can replay at home and see exactly what happens on a shoot.

Summary:
We live in an age where innovative technology is being developed, implemented and evolved at a dizzying rate, and in South Africa, very few technology focused products are easily available to developers and consumers alike. The Oculus Rift is one such technology which hasn’t been examined and tested for the South African market, until now.

SDK Digital Lab is the first South African agency to be working with and developing for the Oculus Rift and other Virtual Reality devices, with added focus on educating the South African market about the technology and its benefits.

While VR has received a substantial amount of attention globally in the field of gaming, this technology could change the way that we experience the world beyond games and will have the greatest impact in areas like leisure, travel, entertainment and education. Expensive rigs are out of reach for most local people so SDK Africa is focussing on developing tech for Google cardboard and mobile solutions.

From K53 driver training for new drivers to virtual field trips for disabled and distant students, we investigate the cutting edge tech that being developed on our shores. SDK Africa has offices in Johannesburg, Cape Town, Cameroon and San Francisco and is the only VR company in Africa with foreign investment, however there are other companies rushing to develop content locally and abroad.

Will show how 360 rigs are used, have a presenter wearing a visor and sharing their experience and potentially other wearable / haptic items should time allow.

Further information:
Interviews with Shaun Wilson - MD, SDK Africa
Learners currently using the tech
Input from Playstation about their Playstation VR
Input from Oculus Rift / Facebook
Input from Google and Google cardboard

Press Release:


Immersive Technology
Virtual reality technology is revolutionizing the way designers, architects and artists create. From K53 driver training to virtual field trips for disabled and distant students,
this cutting-edge, locally developed technology is transforming education in schools and training in the workplace. Carte Blanche looks at the world through a different
lens.

Script:


VR AND IMMERSION TECH
06/04/2017

Producer: James Carroll
Journo: Claire Mawisa


CLAIRE
The age of virtual reality is upon us and we’re seeing the world through a different lens.

CLAIRE VO
Virtual Reality technology or VR is revolutionizing how designers, architects and artists work and how the rest of us experience their art.

Entire worlds can live inside computers, ready to share and experience instantaneously. This level of freedom grants the user unparalleled immersion that they wouldn’t perceive from a flat two-dimensional screen.

Take architecture for example: while the vast majority of architects have adopted 3D modeling, new applications for VR platforms like Oculus Rift, HTC Vive and Google Cardboard are enabling them to walk around their buildings before the first brick is laid.

South Africa is not far behind the new developments. Shaun Wilson is the MD of AwakenVR, a company specializing in virtual reality.

CLAIRE
Shaun, what are these? What are we sitting in?

SHAUN
These are called Ocupods, we came up with them last year to house people in virtual reality experiences because generally when people are sitting in an open chair, they don’t feel comfortable so we made these for events and conferences but now we’re looking at putting these in households.

CLAIRE
What is the difference between 360 and VR?

SHAUN
Virtual reality is a simulated environment where 360 is a capture of a real-world environment so with VR you can manipulate your scenes and engage where with 360 you’re more in a voyeurism role.

CLAIRE
What are the benefits of virtual reality?

SHAUN
There are multiple benefits. For instance, in Africa, most people don’t get to travel. Now 360 video allows you to explore without leaving your home or your room and you can do that for R95 with a piece of Google cardboard so anyone has the experience to go anywhere in the world. I’m sure you’ve been fortunate enough to travel so that isn’t something that appeals to you but if you have got a fear of heights or skydiving 360 can help you overcome that fear because you can relive that moment over and over again until you’re comfortable with it. The same goes for the fear of flying, PTSD - 360 isn’t just a fad - it’s going to become a way of life.

CLAIRE
So, I think the best way to describe it is to actually experience it.

SHAUN
Yes, so we actually have a couple of pieces on here that we shot. One of the most popular pieces is standing on the field for the national anthem at the Springbok game which is an experience that very few people get to have.

CLAIRE
I’m on the field!
My heart it actually pounding!
It’s actually quite an emotional experience.

CLAIRE VO
And while we can’t accurately show you what it’s like to be in the immersive world of 360 with our Springboks, we can assure you the experience was breath-taking!

CLAIRE
That was magic. That was absolutely magical. Sho – it really transports you into another world and you would think because it’s on a phone and it’s a headset, will I really be able to feel what they’re feeling, but you do… that’s what so impressive.

CLAIRE
The virtual big had bitten hard so to compare 360 with a VR experience, Ebrahim Naidoo at Nexus gave me a taste using an HTC Vive complete with full body motion tracking and controllers.

CLAIRE
Again, we can’t properly show what it was like to be in the virtual world but we brought back a souvenir.

CLAIRE
That’s just incredible, I’m just blown away – I’m amazing. I didn’t know I was such a good artist you guys.

CLAIRE VO
The immersion experience that headsets provide is far superior to basic book or manual learning. Employers may have previously used Powerpoint presentations to emphasize the importance of safety - they can now put their employees at the heart of the proceedings. Trainees can use VR to practice essential skills without placing their lives at risk.

By setting aside the manuals and worksheets, trainees also stand a better chance of retaining information. The importance of experiential learning has long been recognized in many professions but now research suggests it helps with more abstract learning too. With users able to rewind training and progress at their own pace, VR systems can also combat our shrinking attention spans. So why hasn’t this technology been more widely adopted?

SHAUN
The biggest problem with VR now is that everyone assumes it’s for gaming and that’s one of the things that we’re trying to debunk because at the end of the day VR is not the future for Africa, 360 is.

CLAIRE
How is that the best option for Africa?

SHAUN
It’s because of the high costs. If you need to pay R15,000 for a headset and between R20-R30,000 for a machine in order to run an Oculus Rift the majority of the people can’t afford it. Because everyone in Africa has got a cellphone and the majority of cellphones can do 360, that’s why we see it as a bigger market.

CLAIRE VO
Redhill School in Johannesburg is embracing this technology by supplementing existing classes with solutions like Google cardboard.
Philip Joubert is the director of STEM and Innovation at the school.

PHILIP
With the advent of really cheap entry to mobile technology, that’s where we are finding the sweet spot because nowadays most of the kids, especially in well resourced schools have got access to smart devices and we can utilize them. We don’t have to purchase any additional equipment and Google has been really really great in getting into the educational space there so if it’s something that everyone can directly experience – that’s great.

CLAIRE
What could you share with me that you’ve experienced in VR that you know that you would not normally experience in real life?

GIRL
We saw polar bears, the Aurora Borealis… I mean some people will never get to see that but with VR you see it and you feel like you’re right there.

CLAIRE
I’m a mother to a 12 year old and I saw the kids there having lots of fun, how do I know he’s actually learning something?

PHILIP
The issue is with the experience of learning that you and I went through. We’ve got a very particular image in our minds and a big part of our job here is to convince parents that learning in some way is taking place, that learning has got a different flavor to what you and I experienced.

BOY
My parents are like VR, games now? Why are you playing games in class - this is not allowed. So I show them that this is what we do and they begin to understand more and more what VR can actually do. Because my parents are like uh-uh, no devices, paper, black and white.

CLAIRE
Is VR in education sustainable?

PHILIP
Okay, that’s a very good question because there is the assumption that new and shiny technology will immediately make kids more interested and elevate the educational experience. And unless it’s done particularly well, we thing that technology can also distract from the real thorough learning.

CLAIRE VO
The pupils at this particular school seem to have assimilated easily into using 360 environments for studying. We decided to see what the response would be for first time users.

GIRL
That was awesome.

CLAIRE
Who wants to tell me what they watched and how was that experience for them?

BOY
You went on the rollercoaster and when you turned upsound down it gave you a weird feeling – it felt like you were turning even though you weren’t.

GIRL
It’s amazing how technology can take you into a different world like you’re not in this room anymore, that you’re somewhere else and things are different.

CLAIRE VO
Philip feels that we’re only starting to scratch the surface of what is possible but with new methodologies comes a new way to assess results.

PHILIP
The big misconception we’re finding when most people talk about VR educational technology is that VR is a way of consuming content and we actually want the kids producing content and that’s a slightly different model on things because we actually want kids to be innovative, creative and collaborative.

CLAIRE
Don’t you think it’s a bit isolating?

SHAUN
Yes, you can have isolated moments which is a problem, but it also allows those people who are introverts to start engaging with people on social platforms because they can now actually “be there” which is another benefit because you get a lot of individuals that don’t leave their house, but now with VR they can go anywhere.

CLAIRE
What challenges are you facing?

SHAUN
Because the technology is so new, finding the skillset is very difficult. For us with our work it’s becoming harder and harder to find the right skill so what we’re doing now is recruiting students directly out of school in their final year so that we can massage how we want them to work in a VR environment.

PHILIP
South African education is a two-tier system, there are private schools, quintel 5 schools or former model c schools and they don’t mind curriculum changes or changes from MECs, they get on with it and get really good exam results – the issue is the schools that are under-resourced and ones of the goals here is to make the mistakes. I think there is an ethical and moral imperative for private schools to use their resources, make the expensive mistakes and then develop a model that can be rolled out at a fraction of the cost.

CLAIRE
So while the rate of the general public’s adoption of VR is uncertain, it’s clear that the technology is spurring rapid innovation in art, design, education and entertainment.

CLAIRE VO
Watch this space - over the next couple of years the lines between this reality and those generated inside computers will continue to blur.




PROMOS

1. 15”
Virtual Reality technology or VR is revolutionizing how designers, architects and artists work and how the rest of us experience their art. We dive deep into the virtual world to see how this is influencing education.

GIRL UP SOUND
Awesome


2. 15”
Travel all over the world is now possible through your mobile device and some cardboard googles. Carte Blanche investigates the limitless possibilities of virtual reality.

CLAIRE UP SOUND
I’m on the field!


3. 10”
Science and education is now merging in the virtual realm. How will this change learning in the future?
